findings.title: Failed save destroys the pre-existing file at that path (truncate-on-open, no atomic write)
findings.description: save() opens fname with open(fname, 'wb') BEFORE pickling, so the target file is truncated to 0 bytes first. If pickle.dump then fails (any unpicklable member: open file handle, lambda, locally-defined function, HyperAnimation...), the user's previous good file at that path is destroyed. Verified: an 8152-byte file previously written by hyp.save was truncated to 0 bytes by a failed re-save and became unloadable (EOFError: Ran out of input). Failed saves to new paths also leave corrupt partial files behind (0 bytes for early failures; 65549 bytes for a HyperAnimation that failed mid-dump), which later hyp.load calls trip over. Realistic scenario: a scientist re-saves an updated results dict over yesterday's results file; one member is unpicklable; the exception also silently destroys yesterday's results. Standard fix: pickle to a temp file (or pickle.dumps to bytes) first, then atomically rename/write.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, os, hypertools as hyp
f = '/tmp/precious_results.pkl'
hyp.save(np.arange(1000, dtype=float), f)   # yesterday's good results
print(os.path.getsize(f))                    # 8152
bad = {'results': np.arange(1000.), 'log': open('/etc/hosts', 'rb')}
try:
    hyp.save(bad, f)                         # raises TypeError
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e)
print(os.path.getsize(f))                    # 0  <- old file destroyed
hyp.load(f)                                  # EOFError: Ran out of input
findings.expected: A failed save leaves the previous file contents intact (write-to-temp + rename), or at minimum documents that the target is truncated before serialization.
findings.actual: CASE X-failed-save-destroys-existing-file: save raised [TypeError: cannot pickle 'BufferedReader' instances]; file size 8152 -> 0; old file NO LONGER LOADABLE: EOFError: Ran out of input | CASE X-failed-anim-save-partial: failed animation save leaves 65549-byte partial file

findings.title: save() writes pickle bytes regardless of extension: .npy/.csv/.json/.xlsx/... files are unreadable by their nominal tools, with no warning
findings.description: hyp.save(obj, 'data.npy'|'data.csv'|'data.json'|'data.xlsx'|'data.mat'|'data.parquet'|...) silently writes a pickle. The sibling hyp.load() parses those same extensions properly when reading genuine files, and only round-trips hyp.save output because _load_local sniffs the pickle magic byte (b'\x80'). External tools fail on the masquerading files: np.load('data.npy') -> ValueError ('This file contains pickled (object) data...'), pd.read_csv('data.csv') -> UnicodeDecodeError ('0x80 in position 0'). A scientist who saves 'results.csv' to share with a collaborator (or Excel/R) gets an unreadable file and no warning. All 15 tested extensions round-trip through hyp.load, so within-hypertools behavior is consistent, but the load/save format asymmetry is a trap. Suggest: warn (or raise) when fname has a known non-pickle data extension, or implement format-aware writing (see F20-save-010).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
arr = np.arange(12, dtype=float).reshape(4, 3)
hyp.save(arr, '/tmp/data.npy')
print(open('/tmp/data.npy','rb').read(2))   # b'\x80\x04' -- a pickle, not npy
np.load('/tmp/data.npy')                     # ValueError
hyp.save(arr, '/tmp/data.csv')
import pandas as pd; pd.read_csv('/tmp/data.csv')  # UnicodeDecodeError
findings.expected: Either the file format matches the extension, or save warns/raises for recognized data-format extensions it does not honor.
findings.actual: np.load: 'ValueError: This file contains pickled (object) data. If you trust the file you can load it unsafely using the `allow_pickle=` keyword argument or `pickle.load()`.' | pd.read_csv: "UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 0: invalid start byte" | hyp.load round-trips all 15 extensions exactly (magic=b'\x80\x04' each)

findings.title: Round-trip silently returns a different object for anything exposing .get_data(): saved Line2D comes back as a tuple of arrays
findings.description: load() ends with 'return geo_data.get_data() if hasattr(geo_data, "get_data") else geo_data' (hypertools/io/load.py line 332), intended for legacy DataGeometry unpickling. But it fires for ANY unpickled object with a get_data attribute. Verified: hyp.save(matplotlib Line2D) then hyp.load returns tuple (array([1,2,3]), array([4,5,6])) instead of the Line2D. Any user class with a get_data() method is likewise silently transformed. This breaks the save/load identity contract with no error or warning. Suggested fix: isinstance(geo_data, DataGeometry) check instead of duck-typed hasattr.

findings.title: save() accepts and silently ignores ALL keyword arguments (protocol=, compress=, format=, typos)
findings.description: The signature is save(obj, fname, **kwargs) but kwargs are never used. hyp.save(arr, f, protocol=0), compress=True, format='npy', and banana=42 all produce byte-identical default-protocol pickles with no error or warning. A user who requests protocol=0 (or 5, or compression, or a format) believes it took effect. Silent-swallow also hides typos of would-be options. Should either honor protocol (pass through to pickle.dump) or drop **kwargs so unexpected kwargs raise TypeError.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
arr = np.arange(12.).reshape(4, 3)
hyp.save(arr, '/tmp/kw1.pkl')
hyp.save(arr, '/tmp/kw2.pkl', protocol=0, compress=True, format='npy', banana=42)
print(open('/tmp/kw1.pkl','rb').read() == open('/tmp/kw2.pkl','rb').read())  # True
findings.expected: Unknown kwargs raise TypeError; protocol= (at least) is honored.
findings.actual: CASE K-kwargs-silently-ignored: PASS -- ALL kwargs silently ignored: protocol=0/compress/format='npy'/banana=42 produce byte-identical pickle; no error, no warning

findings.title: Corrupt/truncated pickle written by hyp.save produces misleading ('DataGeometry ... pass legacy=True') or bare (EOFError) load errors
findings.description: Two failure shapes for the save->load round-trip when the file is damaged (interrupted write, disk full -- which save itself can cause, see F20-save-001): (a) a pickle with garbage after the header raises HypertoolsIOError 'Failed to load DataGeometry object from <path>. If <name> was created with hypertools<0.8.0, pass legacy=True to load it.' -- DataGeometry is a pre-1.0 internal concept and legacy=True would not help a 1.0 hyp.save file; the message sends users down a dead end. (b) a 0-byte file raises bare 'EOFError: Ran out of input' with no filename or hypertools context, because io/load.py line 346 only catches pickle.UnpicklingError and EOFError is not a subclass. Suggested: catch Exception around pickle.loads and emit one message naming the path and stating the file appears truncated/corrupted.

open('/tmp/trunc.pkl','wb').write(b'\x80\x04TRUNC')
hyp.load('/tmp/trunc.pkl')   # HypertoolsIOError about DataGeometry/legacy=True
open('/tmp/empty.pkl','wb').close()
hyp.load('/tmp/empty.pkl')   # bare EOFError: Ran out of input
findings.expected: A single clear error: file appears truncated or corrupted, with the path, and no misleading legacy=True suggestion for files that were never DataGeometry pickles.
findings.actual: HypertoolsIOError: Failed to load DataGeometry object from .../truncated.pkl. If truncated.pkl was created with hypertools<0.8.0, pass legacy=True to load it. | EOFError: Ran out of input (0-byte file, no path in message)

findings.title: 1.0 public API docs for hypertools.save are a single sentence; kwargs, return value, pickle format, and security warning all undocumented
findings.description: hyp.save.__doc__ == 'Pickle `obj` to `fname`.' -- no Parameters, Returns, or Examples sections, unlike every other public hypertools function. docs/hypertools.save.rst is '.. autofunction:: save', so the rendered 1.0 docs page shows only that sentence. Not documented: (a) the accepted obj types (module docstring lists 'array / DataFrame / list / fitted model' but autofunction does not render module docstrings); (b) that **kwargs are accepted-and-ignored (F20-save-005); (c) that the format is always pickle regardless of extension (F20-save-002) and which extensions hyp.load will round-trip; (d) the do-not-unpickle-untrusted-files security note (present only in the module docstring; hyp.load's docstring DOES carry a pickle warning); (e) return value (None). Also the module docstring NOTE says the format-aware exporter 'lands in Plan 6 (plot)' and 'comes later' -- plot(save_path=...) has since landed (plot.py lines 2713-2718), so the internal note is stale for the 1.0 release.
findings.expected: A numpydoc docstring with Parameters/Returns/Examples, a pickle-security note, and cross-references to hyp.load round-trip behavior and plot(save_path=...) for figures.

findings.title: save() surfaces raw unbranded OS/pickle errors while load() wraps failures in HypertoolsIOError; no auto-mkdir for nested paths
findings.description: Every save failure mode is a bare builtin exception with no hypertools context or remedy: missing parent dirs -> FileNotFoundError (no auto-mkdir and no hint to create them); directory as fname -> IsADirectoryError; read-only dir -> PermissionError; fname=None or swapped args -> TypeError 'expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not ndarray'; unpicklable obj -> AttributeError/TypeError from pickle internals. The sibling load() wraps its failures in HypertoolsIOError with attempted-resolution digests. Inconsistent error-surface for the two halves of the same round-trip API.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.arange(3), '/tmp/no/such/dir/f.pkl')   # FileNotFoundError
hyp.save('/tmp/f.pkl', np.arange(3))                # TypeError (swapped args)
findings.expected: HypertoolsIOError (or at least messages) naming the problem and the fix, consistent with load().
findings.actual: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../no/such/dir/data.pkl' | IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] | PermissionError: [Errno 13] | TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not ndarray | AttributeError: Can't get local object 'k_unpicklable.<locals>.<lambda>'

findings.title: No format-aware export: load() reads 12+ formats, save() writes exactly one (pickle)
findings.description: hyp.load parses .npy/.npz/.csv/.tsv/.txt/.json/.parquet/.mat/.xlsx/.xls plus pickles, URLs, and hosted datasets, but hyp.save can only emit pickle. Scientists routinely need to hand results to R/MATLAB/Excel collaborators; today they must bypass hypertools (df.to_csv, np.save, ...). An extension-driven writer (mirroring load's extension table) for arrays/DataFrames would close the loop, and is a natural companion to fixing F20-save-002. Also missing: protocol=/compression options.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.eye(3), '/tmp/m.csv')  # writes a pickle named .csv; no way to write real csv
findings.expected: save(obj, 'x.csv') writes CSV (etc.), or a format= parameter exists.
findings.actual: All extensions produce pickle bytes (magic b'\x80\x04'); see F20-save-002 verbatim outputs.
